title: In 1859, a Solar Storm Set Telegraph Paper on Fire

scenes.text: In 1859, the Sun made telegraph paper catch fire.
On September 1, astronomer Richard Carrington saw a bright flash on the Sun.
A day later, a massive solar storm hit Earth.
Telegraph operators got shocked, and paper in some offices caught fire.
Auroras reached as far south as Cuba, the Bahamas and Jamaica.
Some skies glowed bright enough to read a newspaper.

description:
In September 1859 a huge solar storm hit Earth, shocking telegraph operators and setting paper in some offices on fire.
Auroras reached as far south as Cuba, the Bahamas and Jamaica.
What would a storm like that do today?
thumbnail_text: THE SUN SET PAPER ON FIRE
first_comment: A storm like this hit in 1859. What do you think it would break today?
